_doc: Markets added in kit v2.1 (2026-11-18), read by kit/costs.py beside lab/r2/fp_costs.json (never edited). Same fields as fp_costs.json plus: provisional (true: the broker's own figures are not read yet; judge.verdict writes PROVISIONAL COSTS), source (where each figure comes from), spread_bps (spread in bp of the trade's price, instead of spread/spread_ref_price), commission_per_unit (price units per unit per side, charged on top of the half spread on each side, x1.5 in the stress, 0 in gross; split-adjusted by data.split_factor in sim.Book), min_commission_per_side (reported, not modelled), min_day_bars (bars a 17:00-NY day needs to count in D20), local (prepared hourly bars only, no download), data_symbol, ref_price (rough in-sample median close, a decoding magnitude check only), splits {ex-date: ratio} and splits_checked_to (the prepared bars are NOT split-adjusted; data.load_bars back-adjusts them). Kit v2.1 fix (2026-11-18): spread_abs (oil: spread in USD per unit, constant, scaled only by the roll adjustment), spread_bps_by_year (shares: the level used for a bar of that New York year; spread_bps is used for years not listed), min_commission_per_side is MODELLED at the stake notional (_stake), min_bar_minutes (shares: bars with fewer minutes are dropped by data.load_bars), rolls {reopen time UTC: ratio} and rolls_checked_to (oil: data.load_bars back-adjusts the futures contract rolls), dividends {ex-date: dividend / previous close}, dividends_checked_to and dividend_credit_long (shares).

source.rolls: kit v2.1 fix 2 (verifier KF-1, KF-7): the data (Dukascopy LIGHT.CMD/USD) is the FRONT WTI future, switched once a month by the vendor to the next contract. Listed: one roll a month 2013-01 to 2021-12 (108): key = the first bar (UTC) on the new contract, value = ratio next / front. Both come from OUTSIDE settlements, not from the bars' reopen gap (which includes the real move of the night, or of a data hole): EIA daily NYMEX WTI settlements of contract 1 (front, until its last trading day) and contract 2 (RCLC1, RCLC2; rows before 2022 only) against Dukascopy's mid at 14:28-14:30 New York (the settlement window). Dating: Dukascopy is on contract 2 on a day when its price is closer to C2 than to C1 (days with |log(C2/C1)| < 12 bp say nothing); the roll is the reopen (first bar after a break of >= 1.75 h) between the last day on C1 and the first day of the final run on C2 before the expiry (after the expiry when Dukascopy is still on C1 that day); several reopens: Dukascopy's usual one (18:00 New York before trading day E in 2015-09..2019-12, before trading day E-1 otherwise), else the first after the expiry, else the one whose gap is closest to the outside spread. Ratio = C2 / C1 settled on the last day whose 14:30 settlement precedes the end of the last front-month bar, so the real move after the settlement and over the night stays in the series. Scripts: kit_v21/fix2/s/k1_level.py, k1_fetch_eia.py, k1_build.py (k1_build.json gives each month's case, interval and candidates), k1_compare.py. The outside data are kept in kit/oil_outside.csv for the real-bars check. rolls_vendor_gap = the vendor's raw reopen move at each listed roll (open / previous close of the raw bars), used by data.check_adjusted to refuse raw bars. After rolls_checked_to the kit applies the rule E-1 with the ratio measured on the bars (README limits: that ratio includes the night's real move; a reopen after a hole raises).
source.contango: with the rolled (back-adjusted) series, the futures carry (contango / backwardation) is IN THE PRICE path, as for a CFD on the future rolled by price adjustment; the swaps (6 % long, 4 % short, both a cost) are a financing guess ON TOP, so the carry is counted once through the price plus a pessimistic swap. If FP's XTIUSD is a spot CFD whose swap carries the contango, the real swap replaces the guess; read it in MT5 (symbol specification, swap long / short).

source.spread_bps: levels for years NOT listed (2022 on): spread_bps = max(2021 level, mean of the yearly levels) of the 10-15 group, spread_bps_h09 the same for the 09 bar's open
source.spread_bps_by_year: kit v2.1 fix 2 (KF-5): TWO levels per New York calendar year, each calibrated on its own minutes: spread_bps_by_year for the open of the 10-15 bars (hh:00 minutes) and every bar close, spread_bps_by_year_h09 for the open of the 09:00-labelled bar (the 09:30 first minute). Each level is set so that the kit's mean spread (level x the whole-period hour-of-week shape of extra_shape.json) over that group's bar-open minutes of the year EQUALS the mean quoted spread of the lab's one-minute bid/ask at those minutes (read with ts < 2022): kit_v21/fix2/s/k5_levels.py (from the one-level table of the first fix, whose pooled mean was exact but whose groups were off by 0.51-1.62 (10-15) and 0.75-2.16 (09)), k5_install.py
source.dividends: Yahoo chart API events (period2 2021-12-31, only events dated before 2022 read), stored as dividend / previous session close, so no later split adjustment is kept; a SHORT open at the ex-date's first bar (09:30 New York) pays frac x its fill price; a long is credited dividend_credit_long x that (0: credits ignored, as swaps; to read at FP)
source.commission_per_unit: V21-8: 0.03 USD per share per side in net (DailyForex review, MT5: 0.03; FP's fees page snippet: 0.02), 0.045 in the stress, 0 in gross; the 2 USD minimum per side is MODELLED at the stake notional (V21-2, _stake)
source.min_bar_minutes: V21-7: a share bar with fewer than 5 one-minute rows (volume column) is dropped by data.load_bars: the one-minute 13:00 bar of a half day, partial hours of data holes
source.dividend_credit_long: kit v2.1 fix 2 (KF-4): a LONG open at an ex-date's first bar is credited 70 % of the dividend (x its fill): share CFD brokers credit longs with the dividend, often net of the 30 % US withholding tax that applies without a treaty rate; 0.70 is the pessimistic end of the usual 70-100 % (decision not the fixer's: the pessimistic side is taken). To read in MetaTrader / FP's dividend policy. judge.verdict reports the long result at credits 0 and 1 as well (results.json 'dividends'). A short pays 100 %
